items.title: Palworld picks spin-offs over a Fortnite-style metaverse because "maximizing revenue as quickly as possible isn’t what drives our creative decisions," says Pocketpair lead
items.summary: The devs are simply driven by whether something sounds cool
items.content:
The devs are simply driven by whether something sounds cool

(Image credit: Pocketpair) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The Palworld universe is expanding quite a bit in the coming months. Developer and publisher Pocketpair has got a dating sim, a farming sim, and an MMO on the slate, and while you might think elements of these would make more sense as expansions of the main game, the team isn't keen on simply replicating Fortnite's metaverse-type model.

"I can certainly understand why some people might expect us to take Palworld in that direction," John 'Bucky' Buckley, the head of publishing and communications at Pocketpair, tells MP1st . "But for us, we just want to make fun games in our own way. I know it sounds a bit cliché, but while we obviously want our games to be successful, maximizing revenue as quickly as possible isn’t what drives our creative decisions."

Indeed, given the fervent community around Palworld, there's been plenty of opportunity to turn the game into a money-making machine through crossovers and microtransactions and whatever. But the biggest purchase remains simply buying the monster-collecting experience, and it's a model that's working for all involved thus far.

Watch On In keeping separate ideas just that and making them their own games, it allows Pocketpair to explore the mechanics involved and create disparate projects that may be more attractive to other players. "When it comes to Palworld, we feel that some ideas would be better served as standalone games, where we can fully design the gameplay systems, pacing, and overall experience around that specific concept," Buckley adds.

"Palfarm is a good example. Rather than trying to fit that experience into Palworld as just one mode, we believe making it a standalone title gives it more room to develop its own identity and become something special in its own right," he continues. "We don’t see this as one approach being better than the other. Different games and IPs will naturally benefit from different strategies."

Palworld's cursed dating sim is a "little goofy thing" and not a proper spin-off, Pocketpair lead says Pocketpair lead says "TemTem are not our rivals" as it gets its own Palworld-like survival game "Many people" tried securing a Palworld collab and failed, lead says, but Pocketpair isn't unique The resistance to homogeneity is refreshing, and it's likely to be a real strength in years to come. It allows Palworld to exist in multiple different forms, so if one starts to wane for whatever reason, others are there to help hoist the overall property. The Fortnite model of having everything in the same platform places a lot of emphasis on one audience, a plan that could leave you high and dry one day.

On Twitter , just to double-down on his responses here, Buckley reiterated that Pocketpair is completely independent. "I understand that the astronomical success of Palworld has blurred the public’s perception of what Pocketpair actually is, but we are, in fact, still 100% self-owned and more importantly, 100% self-funded," he states.

items.title: Pocketpair shares stance on Palworld spin-off games and why a live-service format with tons of DLC “is not the right way forward for us”
items.summary: Pocketpair’s monster-taming survival title Palworld has been a sensation ever since its Early Access launch in 2024, and continues to enjoy popularity among gamers following its recent 1.0 launch. The company has since expanded its horizons, launching its own indie game publishing division called Pocketpair Publishing in January 2025, and Palworld’s own official TCG in August 2026. While the Palworld IP is also set to expand through spin-off games like Palworld: Palfarm and Pal♡world! ~More Than Just Pals~, the developers aren’t necessarily keen on continuing to expand Palworld itself in a live-service fashion. In a recent interview with MP1st, John “Bucky” Buckley, Pocketpair’s Head of Publishing and Communications, shared the […]
items.content:
Home News Pocketpair shares stance on Palworld spin-off games and why a live-service format with tons of DLC “is not the right way forward for us” Game Development , News 2026-10-14 19:08 Akira Sada Pocketpair’s monster-taming survival title Palworld has been a sensation ever since its Early Access launch in 2024, and continues to enjoy popularity among gamers following its recent 1.0 launch. The company has since expanded its horizons, launching its own indie game publishing division called Pocketpair Publishing in January 2025, and Palworld’s own official TCG in August 2026. While the Palworld IP is also set to expand through spin-off games like Palworld: Palfarm and Pal♡world! ~More Than Just Pals~, the developers aren’t necessarily keen on continuing to expand Palworld itself in a live-service fashion.

In a recent interview with MP1st , John “Bucky” Buckley, Pocketpair’s Head of Publishing and Communications, shared the company’s stance on the matter.

When asked why Palworld hasn’t adopted a more metaverse-style format akin to Fortnite (like, for instance, integrating Palfarm into Palworld itself as a new mode), Bucky commented, “I can certainly understand why some people might expect us to take Palworld in that direction, but for us… we just want to make fun games in our own way. I know it sounds a bit cliché, but while we obviously want our games to be successful, maximizing revenue as quickly as possible isn’t what drives our creative decisions.” Over on X, Bucky added , “We could probably turn Palworld into a big live-service game with tons of DLC and MTX, but I don’t think it’s the right way forward for us.”

He presented Palworld: Palfarm as an example of this policy, stating that the team felt some ideas were best kept as standalone titles. Rather than making a farming side mode within Palworld, Pocketpair believes a dedicated farming game has more room to develop its own mechanics and concepts without being constrained by the needs of the main game.

Bucky also offered his own take on how the metaverse format has proven itself well for games such as Fortnite, saying that while he acknowledges that it works well for Epic Games, “We don’t see this as one approach being better than the other,” and concluded that different IPs will naturally adopt different strategies.

In his personal X post promoting the MP1st article, Bucky noted that Pocketpair is not as financially motivated as people may assume, adding that the company is 100% self-owned and self-funded, which means its decision-making process revolves largely around what the devs themselves find fun.

He also reiterated to MP1st that “The main Palworld game remains extremely important to us, and these spin-offs are not intended to replace it. We see them as new ways for players to enjoy the world and characters of Palworld from different perspectives.”

Palworld is out now for PC ( Steam /Microsoft Store/Mac App Store), PS5, and Xbox Series X/Xbox One. The game is also available via Game Pass for PC and Xbox. Two spin-off titles, Palworld: Palfarm and Pal♡world! ~More Than Just Pals~ have also been revealed, with release dates TBA.

Related: Pocketpair’s first open-world survival game Craftopia finally set for full release next year. Post-Palwolrd success helped the devs tackle longstanding technical issues

items.title: Palworld Devs on Standalone Spinoffs: “Maximizing Revenue” Isn’t What Drives Creative Decisions
items.summary: Palworld has spinoffs announced, but wouldn't it make more sense to have these integrated into the game like Fortnite? Pocketpair answers.
items.content:
One of the biggest surprise hits in recent memory has to be Palworld . Pocketpair came out of nowhere, and while initially thought of as a Pokémon clone, the game has proven it has its own identity.

It’s gotten so big, in fact, that Pocketpair decided to spin it off with a new project called Palworld: Palfarm, which is due for release on PC — at least initially. But wouldn’t it have made more sense for Pocketpair to integrate Palfarm into the main Palworld game? Similar to what Fortnite has done to build a metaverse with the likes of LEGO, Rocket Racing and other IPs and genres.

Speaking to MP1st in an exclusive interview, we asked Palworld about the brand’s spinoffs, and they’re not leaning toward building more of a metaverse-type experience.

Answering for Pocketpair is John “Bucky” Buckley, the studio’s Head of Publishing and Communications.

Save 5% on your next top-up, games, gift cards, and virtual currency at Eneba. Use code MP1ST5 at checkout.

MP1st : We know multiple spinoffs are coming, with Palfarm being one of them. It seems the studio is pressing hard on the accelerator to expand the IP’s footprint. That makes sense given the success, but the online gaming landscape has been leaning toward building more of a metaverse-type experience, with Fortnite being the biggest example.

Bucky answered, “Well… I can certainly understand why some people might expect us to take Palworld in that direction, but for us… we just want to make fun games in our own way. I know it sounds a bit cliché, but while we obviously want our games to be successful, maximizing revenue as quickly as possible isn’t what drives our creative decisions.”

Bucky continued and used Palfarm as an example, stating, “When it comes to Palworld, we feel that some ideas would be better served as standalone games, where we can fully design the gameplay systems, pacing, and overall experience around that specific concept.”

“Palfarm is a good example. Rather than trying to fit that experience into Palworld as just one mode, we believe making it a standalone title gives it more room to develop its own identity and become something special in its own right,” Bucky commented, and acknowledged how what Epic is doing with Fortnite isn’t the wrong way either, adding, “We don’t see this as one approach being better than the other. Different games and IPs will naturally benefit from different strategies.”

Bucky concludes by saying that “For Palworld, this is simply the direction we felt made the most sense. The main Palworld game remains extremely important to us, and these spinoffs are not intended to replace it. We see them as new ways for players to enjoy the world and characters of Palworld from different perspectives.”

Aside from Palfarm, Pocketpair has also announced “Pal♡world! ~More Than Just Pals,” as another spinoff from the main game.

items.title: Azur Promilia, the ‘Palworld Waifu RPG’, Has An English Open Beta Coming Next Year
items.summary: Azur Promilia is an all-new free-to-play RPG with creature companions, and it's getting an English OBT next year.
items.content:
If you thought you were done with creature companion games in the wake of all the new ones hitting the market recently, you might need to make room for one more . Manjuu Games, the creator of Azur Lane, an undeniable gooner game , has confirmed that Azur Promilia, a free, open-world RPG creature companion game with serious furry waifu energy , is getting a new test phase soon-ish.

Next year, an English-version OBT will drop for Azur Promilia, with players getting their hands on the free-to-play cross-platform title that has surpassed a whopping 20 million global pre-registrations. I wonder why…

Azur Promilia is an all-new creature-catching, creature-companion RPG that’s set to land on PlayStation 5, PC, and Mobile platforms. In this game, players find, catch, and bond with ‘Kibo’, cute creatures who assist in combat and with mundane tasks, like farming .

It’s part and parcel of the creature companion gameplay loop , but there’s a twist.

This is a serious gooner game. In a series of images and with a new trailer, Manjuu Games revealed a slate of characters and content for the title, which will launch an Open Beta Test in Summer 2027. It’s bizarre to see a ‘childlike’ game with such voluptuous character models, but there’s a market for it, right?

Azur Promilia | Kibo Safari Kibo are found in every corner of the world, each with its own form and character. Together, they weave the living colors of Promilia. When a shooting star once more cuts across the sky, and one whom no prophecy could name appears, the stories long… pic.twitter.com/NmUF3tj1uC

It’s quite a milestone, as this will be the first time that Azur Promilia has been made available to an English-speaking community. It’s a push towards global support, which is something that we’re seeing more Eastern studios lean towards. Manjuu Games is a Chinese developer, but has a studio in Japan.

Here’s a snippet of the creatures coming to Azur Promilia:

Speaking about the 20 million pre-registration milestone, Manjuu Games said:

Reaching 20 million global pre-registrations is an incredible milestone for our team, and we are deeply grateful for the enthusiasm shown by fans worldwide.

Building on the success of our recent closed beta test in Mainland China, our team is actively working on the English version to ensure a high-quality experience. Establishing our official English channels and announcing our planned Summer 2027 OBT window are key steps in creating a direct, lasting relationship with our global community.

Does Azur Promilia sound like your kind of game? Be honest, and let us know on the Insider Gaming Discord server .

For more Insider Gaming coverage, check out the news that a Walking Dead star has made a Resident Evil movie , and don’t forget to sign up for our newsletter

items.content:
\

Palworld version v1.0.3 has been released!

＝＝＝

\

▼Items and Equipment ・Changed the unlock level of some Jetragon-related technologies from 79 to 70, and reduced the materials required for the Pal Gear used to ride Jetragon.

・Changed the technology unlock level of the Aquatic Construction Kit from Level 66 to Level 23, changed its Ancient Technology Point requirement from 4 to 1, and adjusted the required materials and work amount.

・Extended the duration of World Tree Holy Water.

・Reduced the weight of World Tree Holy Water from 1 to 0.1.

・Added World Tree Holy Water to the rewards for World Tree expeditions, World Tree fishing, and the Large Fishing Pond.

・Increased the amount of World Tree Holy Water obtained from Pals in The World Tree area.

・Increased the amount of World Tree Holy Water obtained from Teafant Spring.

・Adjusted the work amount required to craft the Ancient Armor series.

・Doubled the amount of Fiber obtained from trees.

▼Bases and Missions

・Reduced the building costs of the Crude Oil Extractor, High-Pressure Crude Oil Extractor, and Large Power Generator.

・Increased the crude oil production speed of the Crude Oil Extractor and High-Pressure Crude Oil Extractor.

・The base mission that requires building a Crude Oil Extractor can now also be progressed by building a High-Pressure Crude Oil Extractor.

▼Server Settings

・Added a server setting (bAllowEnemyCampSpawnNearBaseCamp) that disables the suppression of enemy camp spawns near player base camps.

\

▼Graphics and Display

・Adjusted the boundary display in some areas to make it easier to see from a distance.

・Improved the display quality of some objects in dungeons.

▼Sound

・Added a sound effect when using World Tree Holy Water.

\

▼Crashes and Progression Blockers

・Fixed an issue where the mission could become impossible to progress if the barrier was removed before accepting the main mission in Sunreach.

▼Multiplayer and Co-op

・Fixed an issue in co-op where lighting on the client side could display incorrectly after cutscenes or the ending played.

・Fixed an issue in co-op where some scenes could stutter during the cutscene that plays when entering The World Tree.

・Fixed an issue on dedicated servers where Fast Travel could activate unintentionally during Tower Boss battles.

・Fixed an issue on dedicated servers where Pals could appear to vibrate rapidly on the client screen.

▼Pals and NPCs

・Fixed an issue where the summoned Pal could stop fighting.

・Fixed an issue where the summoned Pal could stop helping with base work.

・Fixed an issue in multiplayer where, when the Partner Skill of Orserk or certain other Pals activated, the effect display could fail to update correctly, making it appear as though the skill had not activated.

・Fixed an issue where Alpha Surfent would not produce Leather when assigned to a Ranch.

▼Battles and Bosses

・Fixed an issue where some raid boss battles could fail to progress as intended.

・Fixed an issue where the wave effect and actual damage range did not match for some of Panthalus's attacks.

▼Bases and Building

・Fixed an issue where the placement detection for stairs and slanted roofs could fail to match their actual shape.

・Fixed an issue where stairs could not be placed correctly on the sides of foundations or roofs.

▼Items and Rewards

・Fixed an issue where the reward settings for the normal Moon Lord battle and the Ultra Raid Boss battle had not been updated to the intended settings.

items.title: This New Survival Game Finally Clicked with Me, and I'm Never Looking Back
items.summary: Palworld 1.0 does a great job of easing you into its many complex systems.
items.content:
Survival games have been wildly popular for years now. I’ve dabbled here and there to see what the fuss is about, but I’ve always fallen off after a few hours. Usually, I get tangled up in one meagerly explained system after another until I lose track of what I’m supposed to do, and my time with the game peters out.

When Palworld 1.0 came out to rave reviews , I figured I’d give the genre another shot – and I’m glad I did. Palworld’s gradual, newbie-friendly onboarding helped me see what a whole lot of people have loved about survival games all along. Palworld made me a believer.

I’m glad I came in at the 1.0 mark, because I’ve heard Palworld had a much steeper learning curve out of the gate. But now, new players start with a series of missions designed to guide you through the game’s numerous systems . You learn how to punch trees to get wood to create a crafting bench. You learn how to make a club you can use to beat some Pals to death (it’s a dog-eat-dog world out there) to get wool. You then use that wool to make clothes. You set up a camp. You build a house. You activate a teleporter and explore deeper into the game world.

Before long, you’re gliding off cliffs Zelda-style before whomping on every Pal you see to catch them in spheres to put them to work. You can deploy them at your camp, ride them , or have them fight by your side to take on big roaming Pals and towering bosses . It’s a blast. And there’s no way I would have stuck with it if it hadn’t held my hand and eased me into the systems that make up the game.

I still have a long way to go, because I was nowhere near powerful enough to defeat the first boss solo. But those early missions gave me a much-needed handle on what else I can spend my time doing as I level up enough to become a threat. There's a vast world out there I can keep exploring, all while catching Pals and building up my base. I’m having a blast doing it.

Palworld’s 1.0 is available on Steam , Xbox , and PS5 . It costs $29.99, but you can save a few bucks on a Steam copy at Fanatical , which is currently running its summer sale .

Chris Reed is a commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's board game and LEGO coverage. You can follow him on Bluesky .

items.title: Palworld Has Now Outsold Almost Every Mainline Pokémon Game
items.summary: Palworld has reportedly sold 30.5 million copies, surpassing almost every mainline Pokémon game, including Scarlet and Violet
items.content:
Palworld has reportedly sold 30.5 million copies, surpassing almost every mainline Pokémon game, including Scarlet and Violet

X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Share using Native tools Share Copied to clipboard .chargbee-tabs .tab-button .discount{ display:none; } .chargbee-tabs .tab-button .discount .discount-tag{ line-height: 24px !important; } .chargbee-tabs .tab-button.most-popular .join-now-button:hover { background: #000 !important; color: #fff !important; outline: 1px solid #fff !important; } .chargbee-tabs .tab-button .join-now-button:hover { background: 0 0; outline: 1px solid rgba(12, 12, 12, 1); color: rgba(12, 12, 12, 1); } @media (max-width: 1220px){ .chargbee-tabs .tab-button .join-now-button { width: 100% !important; position: unset !important; } } A new report claims that Palworld has sold a staggering 30.5 million units. If accurate, Pocketpair’s controversial survival game has now outsold almost every mainline Pokémon release, including Scarlet and Violet , Sword and Shield , and Gold and Silver .

According to a new report from Alinea Analytics, Palworld has now sold an estimated 30.5 million units across Xbox, PlayStation, and PC . The video game market intelligence firm also estimates that Pocketpair has generated an eye-watering $700 million in total revenue following the recent launch of Palworld 1.0.

If these latest estimates are accurate, they also mean that Palworld has now significantly outsold many of the biggest Pokémon releases over the last 30 years. In Nintendo’s most recent financial report , for example, Pokémon Scarlet and Violet only sold a combined 28.08 million units on Nintendo Switch in comparison.

However, it’s bigger than that, as Palworld has also outsold most classic Pokémon generation titles such as Gold and Silver and Gen 4’s Diamond and Pearl . Here is a full breakdown of the sales figures:

Now, there are a few factors we need to point out here. Since its launch in 1996, the mainline Pokémon series has remained exclusive to Nintendo consoles. One major advantage Palworld has is that it’s an addictive creature-catcher available across most major gaming platforms.

Alinea Analytics points out that while Palworld generated most of its revenue on PC via Steam, it also sold millions of units on PlayStation 5. The game is additionally available on Xbox and through Game Pass, giving it access to a much larger potential audience than an individual Pokémon release.

However, while Palworld has many Pokémon games beat in terms of units sold, Nintendo’s series likely generates more revenue per copy. Pokémon games typically retail for $60 to $70 at launch, while Palworld originally entered early access for $29.99 and has frequently been discounted.

Finally, Nintendo does not update Pokémon sales figures every month, meaning Scarlet and Violet has almost certainly sold additional copies since its last reported total. It’s therefore possible that the Gen 9 games are closer to Palworld than the currently available figures suggest.

Regardless, selling an estimated 30.5 million copies is an incredible achievement for a new IP that only recently debuted in 2024. Palworld is now only around 880,000 units behind Pokémon Red, Green, and Blue , which remains the best-selling mainline Pokémon generation of all time.

items.title: Palworld 1.0 Review – Bigger, Better, and Still Brutally Addictive
items.summary: Palworld 1.0 is crammed with new content. More Pals, better quests, and a fully realized world for new and returning players to explore.
items.content:
Remember Palworld ? Well, the controversial game from Pocketpair finally has a 1.0 release. After two years, this feels like a very different animal than the one I initially encountered. The quest system is more complete, the UI is polished, and the world feels much more interconnected than before. While there are still some rough edges, this version of Palworld is a vastly improved one.

Now, I haven’t been keeping up with every iteration of Palworld released up to this point. So I’m not clear on how gradual or sudden these changes might be. But oh man, the quest system feels like night and day. You’re fed a steady stream of quests from the jump. They pair nicely with the tech tree, they appear on your map, and they sync with your compass. Yes, this is incredibly basic stuff. We figured out quest design decades ago. But you really appreciate the elegance of that design when it’s missing. Then when it finally shows up? It’s water in the desert.

Beyond the quests, it turns out Palworld works much better with connective tissue in place. Fast travel points, side quests, a detailed map, and distant objectives (like a floating island on the horizon) all make the world feel more tangible. Having an objective at all times kept me hooked on the game. Or at least, objectives are perfect for stringing you along until the factory sim element gets its claws in you. Once the big machine gets going, you don’t need anything else to maintain momentum.

The complete list of additions in Palworld 1.0 is downright intimidating. You can read the whole thing on their Steam page, but the highlights are remarkable. 72 new Pals, the Sunreach region, the World Tree, and an increased level cap all speak to a much larger, more complete game. There’s more of course, but the point remains – Palworld has undergone significant changes since the early access days.

This new version of Palworld still has some flaws, to be fair. The laptop I’m using is decently powerful, but I encountered a handful of framerate dips regardless. More important than the tiny performance issues is the core gameplay loop. Things hum along at a more relatable pace than ever before, sure. But you’re still faced with a pretty murderous grind. Pal levels creep upward slowly, and getting through that tech trees gets daunting quite quickly. While things start out breezy enough, the endgame is strictly for simulation psychopaths.

By which I mean the truly dedicated. Which is totally fine! There’s a fascinating disconnect between the monster battling and the base building. You can immerse yourself in one and ignore the other, at least for a hefty chunk of playtime. Although perhaps my impressions of the battling are skewed by hands off it all is. Your Pals run on autopilot, both in battle and beyond it. So for me, the fights are a diversion from my tiny empire.

In that regard, Palworld remains a specialized interest. Either you’re ready to get lost in the details of empire expansion and monster murder, or you’ll quickly lose momentum. The quest system, new content, and expanded Pal roster are all incidental in the face of this essential truth. The gooey caramel center that is the gameplay loop is more or less the same as it ever was. My mind was changed about this game, true. But I’m prone to hyper focus and bouts of mania. So a vast and ruthless machine like Palworld is straight up catnip for my badly wired brain.

The 1.0 release of Palworld presents a very different game than the original early access version. The quest system has been revamped, the map has been expanded, and civilization is scattered everywhere. But the gameplay loop is still pretty relentless. Plus, the rough edges haven’t been completely removed. If the old game was almost it for you, this new iteration might be exactly what you yearned for. But Palworld 1.0 is still an acquired taste.

***A Steam key was provided by the publisher***
